- GPU family fit (H100 vs A100 vs L4) for 70/30 mix of chat/generation
- Sizing for sustained vs burst capacity (hours/day)
- Fallback model variants and expected degradation measures

Hi Ava — thanks for the questionnaire and the context. I pulled together an initial response and a lightweight workbook that maps GPU families to expected sustained tokens/sec and cost-per-token for common model families. See attachments: RFP_Dedicated_Capacity_Response_markus_v1.pdf and nebula_workload_sample_hourly.csv.

Quick highlights from the attachment (summary):
- GPU fit: For a 70/30 chat (low-latency) / long-form (higher throughput) mix we recommend a blended pool: H100s for latency-critical chat paths (p99 < 120ms when packed), A100s for sustained long-form throughput and mixed workloads, and an L4 tier for non-critical prod experiments and embedding backfills.
- Sizing approach: define a baseline "sustained pool" sized to meet 24/7 baseline (average QPS) and a separate "burst pool" sized for 4-hour peak windows. We provide autoscaling with burst lanes and guaranteed burst capacity (reserved + on-demand mix).
- Throughput numbers (example): packed H100 instance (1x) -> ~6k tokens/sec for chat model family X; A100 packed node -> ~18k tokens/sec for decode-heavy models; results vary with sequence length and kv-cache hit rates.
- Tail handling: prefix caching + request-level fallbacks to smaller model variants; expected quality drop quantified in the workbook (BLEU/ROUGE-analog metrics for customer eval prompts).

Next steps I propose: 1) Quick 45-minute sizing workshop to walk through your CSV workload (I can slot aditya_rao from our capacity modeling team), 2) exchange a small sample of production traces (p95/p99 latency histograms) for calibration, 3) finalize a 12-month reserved proposal with tiered burst lanes.

If anything in the attachments doesn't render, tell me and I'll put the workbook in a shared Drive link.

Best,

Ava — thanks for the follow-ups. Paging in Aditya from our capacity modeling team to join the workshop. Answers inline below and in the attached updated workbook (RFP_Dedicated_Capacity_Response_markus_v1.pdf - v2 notes):

1) H100 -> A100 quality delta: for our verified chat family (Model-X-latext), we measured median semantic similarity drop ~0.8 pts and a ~3-5% change in preferred-answer rate when moving from H100 quantized kernels to A100 (same model at reduced kernel parallelism). For most prompts this is minor; for hallucination-sensitive prompts we recommend a canary evaluation set and automatic rollback rules. We'll include exact prompt-level deltas in the workshop workbook.

2) Burst credits: we recommend pooled annual burst credits with monthly allotment flexibility. That matches most enterprise preferences and gives finance predictability. We'll show alternative models (monthly expiry vs pooled) with impact on unit price.

3) Cold-start / KV cache: Redwood's autoscaler supports pre-warm slots and preferred placement to maintain warm KV caches for pinned model versions. For strict p99 targets during sudden scale-ups we recommend a small standing warm pool (configurable) rather than relying on cold-starts. We'll include a suggested warm-pool size in the workbook based on your peak QPS.

Workshop: Tue 2026-12-01 16:00 PST (we'll send an invite). Aditya will lead capacity modeling and I'll take workload-fit and pricing. Please send anonymized p95/p99 histograms and a small sample of request size distribution before EOD Mon 2026-11-30.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
